newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Conservatives get bounce from debates.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Conservatives get bounce from debates.

text.p: Canada's once-mighty Conservatives, struggling to recover from near annihilation in the 1993 federal election, got a substantial bounce from this week's campaign debates, a Reuters poll showed on Friday.

In the first survey released since the debates, voters declared Conservative leader Jean Charest the winner, helping his party cut the lead of Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals by six points. But the Liberals still led the Conservatives, their nearest rivals in the race for the June 2 election, by 25 points, according to the poll conducted for Reuters by Zogby International.

The poll showed momentum for Charest especially in the Atlantic provinces, but as the numbers stand now the Liberals would win re-election. Almost three in 10 voters, however, said they had not made up their minds.

"Despite a very strong performance by Charest in both debates, it clearly doesn't appear it was enough to shake the broad and deep support for the Liberals," said John Zogby, who conducted the poll on May 14 and 15. "However, I think what Charest has done is made the Conservatives a real player for second place."

The poll showed the Liberals leading with 45.4 percent of the decided vote, to 20.4 percent for the Conservatives, 15.8 percent for Reform, 9.9 percent for the New Democratic Party and 7.5 percent for the separatist Bloc Quebecois.

The last Reuters-Zogby poll, taken May 1 to 4, gave the Liberals a 31-point lead over the Conservatives. Analysts have said that the right-wing Reform Party, although trailing the Conservatives nationally, could win more seats and form the official opposition since its strength is concentrated regionally.
